finding: Another build path changed the DLL and the PDB: both hold absolute paths.
The explicit `PathMap` also rewrote `[CallerFilePath]`, which broke the tests' search for the solution folder.
Under Estonian the compiler orders the types it generates for collection expressions differently: 10 of 1237 files. A Roslyn defect, gone on SDK 10.
The WebAPI and job worker images differ in times only. Fixed with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and BuildKit's `rewrite-timestamp`.
Signing gives each of 177 files a timestamped signature, so two signed builds always differ. Check a rebuild by pasting the release's signatures onto it.
Next.js draws a random build ID in every build and writes it into paths and pages: 110 of 998 files. Set to the release version.
Between two commits, the minifier gave other short names in the runtime chunk. Never within one commit, so it does not break reproducibility.
Two machines gave different DLLs from the same source. Both compilers were called 9.0.120, but one was Arch's build of csc and one was Microsoft's.
The release's npm drops the `libc` field from the lock file. It changes which packages install, not the export of one commit.
The MCP images kept files that build steps write as a side effect: font caches, Node's compile cache, test durations. Removed in each step.
The zips differ in every build though every entry's bytes are equal: times, order, modes, owner. Fixed by normalised packing.
The release's version flags reach every assembly. A verifier must know the version string.
